title: Finishing the write sweep
statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite alphabet, let $N\in\mathbb{N}$, let $E$ inject the symbols of $\Gamma$ together with blank into blocks of $N+1$ optional bits, and let $e:\{0,1\}\hookrightarrow\Gamma$ be an embedding. Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over $\Gamma$, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on the letterwise $e$-image of $x$, and let $a$ be an action over $\Gamma$ with the same number of work tapes as $M$. One step of the binary block-code simulator from the write-sweep configuration at counter $0$ equals the move-sweep configuration at counter $N+1$, for the same $c$ and $a$.
hypotheses_covered: $E$ is an injection from symbols of $\Gamma$ together with blank into blocks of $N+1$ optional bits
$M$ is a finite Turing machine over $\Gamma$
$c$ is a configuration on the letterwise $e$-image of $x$
$a$ is an action for the number of work tapes and state type of $M$
replaced:
One transition of the binary block-code simulator applied to the write-sweep
configuration (source configuration $c$, source action $a$) at counter $0$ writes the
last code entry in place and yields the move-sweep configuration at counter $N+1$: the
work tapes now hold the complete blockwise coding of the tapes of the result of
applying $a$ to $c$.
